review_notes: I read the whole target file and the definitions it depends on: `maps` in JointExperiment.lean, `slot` in AnchorTravel.lean, and the earlier uses in MetricService, PrefixAllocation and JointBudget. The file has no `@[simp]` attributes. Most simp calls are `simp only` with explicit lemmas, which is fine. The only real simp-interface gap I found is that the `d < L` / `d ≥ L` branch of `maps`, and the corresponding branch of `selected`, is reduced by hand with `dite_eq_left hj` at many call sites. I did not run Lean. The proposed lemma names and shapes are untested. I did not recommend simp attributes for `key`, `anchor`, `b`, `u`, `c` or `present`, because no use in the file would benefit from unfolding them.

findings.problem: The `d<L` / `d≥L` branch of `JointExperiment.maps` is unfolded by hand each time. Each call is `simpa only [maps,dite_eq_left hj]`, with `hj`, `hd` or `d.isLt` supplied as a proof argument. The same pattern appears at lines 289, 296, 300, 302 and 456, and in MetricService.lean and JointBudget.lean. `maps` has no branch lemmas, only `maps_adapted`. A reader has to unfold the definition each time, and a plain `simp [maps]` cannot discharge the `dite` without an explicit hypothesis.
findings.proposed_change: Next to `maps` in JointExperiment.lean, add two branch lemmas. `maps_of_lt (hd : d < L) : maps law hr s t ω d x = LevelKeys.map s law (hr ⟨d,hd⟩).le ω.val.1 (ω.val.2 ⟨d,hd⟩) t x` and `maps_of_not_lt (hd : ¬ d < L) : maps law hr s t ω d x = Sum.inr x`. Mark them `@[simp]`: simp can discharge the `d < L` side condition from a hypothesis, and for `d.val` with `d : Fin L` through `Fin.is_lt`. Then the call sites become `simpa [maps_of_lt hj] using hz`, or an `rw` with the lemma, and none of them need to unfold `maps`.
findings.benefit: Call sites no longer unfold `maps` by hand. Any later proof about `maps` at a `Fin L` index gets a canonical rewrite. The lemma can also cover the explicit `Sum.inr` case at line 302.

(by simpa only [maps,dite_eq_left hd] using hx) (by simpa only [maps,dite_eq_left hd] using hy)

findings.problem: `selected` is a `dite` on `d<L` with default value `none`. It has no unfolding lemma for in-range `Fin L` indices, and the only bridge to `key`/`anchor` is a one-off `hs` inside `selected_term`. `cutoff_sum` also has to `unfold selected at ha; split_ifs at ha` twice (lines 286–287 and 292–293) because no lemma states the in-range value. The `hs` proof ends in `rfl` after `simp only`, which makes it fragile: it depends on the exact unfolding of `HeavyAnchorDynamics.selected`, `key` and `anchor`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `selected_of_lt (hd : d < L) : selected s law hr t ω y d = HeavyAnchorDynamics.selected s law (r ⟨d,hd⟩) ω.val.1 (ω.val.2 ⟨d,hd⟩).1 t y`. Add a Fin-indexed version `selected_fin (d : Fin L) : selected s law hr t ω y d.val = match key … d y with …`, which is currently the local `hs`. Mark `selected_of_lt` `@[simp]`. Use these in `selected_term` and in the two `unfold selected at ha` blocks of `cutoff_sum`.
findings.benefit: `hs` becomes a reusable lemma. `selected_term` and `cutoff_sum` stop unfolding `selected` and splitting `if`s by hand.
